transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-04
Start time: 09:12 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of AI, Asterion), Ethan Cole (Infra Lead), Sara Valdez (CISO)

Summary:
Quarterly renewal/check-in to confirm Asterion's planned capacity bump (targeting ~2.0x sustained throughput), add EU region for lower latency in customers there, and scope an on-prem/private pilot for regulated workloads. Discussed pricing for 12-month renewal, temporary burst capacity during launch, compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO), and a technical run for 48-hour benchmark. Agreed next steps around pricing and an on-prem architecture workshop.

Topics covered:
- Current throughput and latency baselines
- Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- EU region activation and short pilot sizing
- Contract term options and burst addendum
- Compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot success criteria and rollout plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're on the record. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Nair: Priya here. Morning.
[00:08] Ethan Cole: Ethan, hi.
[00:10] Sara Valdez: Sara, hello.
[00:12] Liam Ortiz: Liam from Redwood.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Cool, thanks. I'll frame why we're here — it's the quarterly renewal check, we saw your growth and you flagged a need for more capacity and an EU region — want to align on numbers and timeline.
[00:29] Priya Nair: Yep, our usage has climbed. The search + dialog path has doubled q/q, and for some EU customers the p99 is spiking, so we need lower latency region and more headroom. We also need a plan for regulated customers where on-prem is required.
[00:44] Ethan Cole: To be specific, right now the service sees about 1.6k RPS at peak, avg token rate about 3.4M tokens/day, and 99th is creeping to 420ms for EU traffic routed through us-west.
[01:04] Liam Ortiz: Thanks Ethan, that matches what our telemetry shows. For the capacity bump — are you thinking committed Dedicated capacity or a Private on-prem pathway? Or hybrid?
[01:15] Priya Nair: Short term we want Dedicated for predictability, but long term we need Private for certain customers — some will require KMS + local audit logs. Can you support a staged approach?
[01:27] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Staged is our recommended approach: Dedicated reserved for baseline, with burst capacity and then a Private pilot to validate SLOs in-region. We can do a 12-month renewal with a ramp schedule.
[01:40] Sara Valdez: A couple of compliance items — we need to see SOC2, ISO27001 docs, and confirm whether Redwood Private integrates with our HSM and the encryption key lifecycle. Also data residency for logs.
[01:54] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM options and support customer-managed keys for Private. Our audit logs can be configured to stay inside the VPC and retained per policy. We'll share the SOC2/ISO zip and a short HSM integration doc after.
[02:06] Ethan Cole: For the EU region, what's the activation lead time? If we commit today, when can you provision a pilot?
[02:13] Maya Chen: If you commit to Dedicated capacity we can stage an EU pilot in 2–3 weeks; full production readiness with routing policies and failover is about 4–6 weeks depending on final sizing and network peering.
[02:27] Priya Nair: Ok, good. Pricing — we want a 12-month term but with a burst addendum for launch spikes. We also want a rollback/fallback to smaller model variants if latency degrades.
[02:40] Maya Chen: We can include a burst bucket as an addendum and set automatic fallback to quantized variants — we call them model variants in the catalog — if latency crosses the SLO. That will be in the pricing sheet.
[02:52] Liam Ortiz: On the technical side, for the pilot we'll recommend KV cache warmup, prefix caching and a batching profile tuned for your request distribution. For on-prem we'll need cluster sizing: GPUs, memory, and local networking.
[03:05] Ethan Cole: Can you recommend a starting configuration? We prefer A100-ish hardware but we can consider L4 for cost.
[03:12] Liam Ortiz: For your current 3.4M tokens/day and 1.6k RPS bursts, a replicated pool of 4x A100 equivalent nodes for Dedicated looks safe with room to autoscale. For Private pilot we can start with 2 nodes to validate and scale to 4 nodes once the 48-hour benchmark passes. L4 variants are great for cost but require quantization and might change quality a bit — we'll run comparisons.
[03:39] Priya Nair: Quality regressions are a concern — our product team will want a comparison report.
[03:44] Liam Ortiz: We'll include a small eval set and a quality/latency tradeoff matrix. We'll run that in the EU pilot.
[03:52] Maya Chen: On contract terms — we can propose three options: 12-month renewal with committed Dedicated + burst, 12-month with a path to Private (pilot included), or an 18-month with better unit pricing. Which direction are you leaning?
[04:05] Priya Nair: 12-month with the Private pathway sounds right. We want flexibility but predictable costs.
[04:11] Sara Valdez: Also want exit criteria for the pilot and data handling SLA spelled out — can't have logs leaving region.
[04:19] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll add explicit pilot acceptance criteria and data residency/retention clauses.
[04:24] Ethan Cole: Network peering — we'll need an architecture call. We have VPCs in eu-west-1 and prefer direct connect.
[04:33] Liam Ortiz: We'll coordinate with your infra team — we'll need IP ranges, expected egress, and peering windows. We'll also provide a template for firewall rules.
[04:44] Priya Nair: Any competition in the mix? We've talked to NimbusAI on pricing and they offered a shorter lead time for EU but didn't offer Private integration the way you do.
[04:56] Maya Chen: Good to know — we find customers trade off lead time vs integration depth. We'll lean into our Private + observability story.
[05:06] Liam Ortiz: On observability — Redwood Console will give token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces. For the pilot we'll enable full retention for 30 days and then roll to your retention policy.
[05:18] Priya Nair: That helps. For the benchmark, can you run a 48-hour production-like replay? We can provide request traces.
[05:25] Liam Ortiz: Yes, a replay is ideal. We'll need a sanitized trace and expected QPS/traffic distribution.
[05:31] Ethan Cole: We'll export a week of traffic and mark the peak windows.
[05:35] Maya Chen: Great. Recap on immediate actions: Maya sends pricing + burst addendum, Liam drafts pilot architecture + sizing, Asterion provides telemetry and compliance points. Any other blockers?
[05:46] Sara Valdez: One more: incident response and SSO. We use Okta; need SAML for admin console and role mappings.
[05:54] Liam Ortiz: Okta SAML is supported for both Hosted and Private. We'll map roles and provide RBAC defaults.
[05:59] Priya Nair: On the topic of fallback models — how transparent is the routing when a fallback happens? We don't want unexpected quality drops without an alert.
[06:07] Liam Ortiz: Fallbacks are policy-driven and surfaced in Redwood Console. We'll configure automatic alerts and optional automatic rollback if quality drops beyond a threshold.
[06:16] Ethan Cole: About quotas — we want a soft quota we can exceed with approval to avoid failed requests during spikes.
[06:23] Maya Chen: We can set a burst bucket and a manual override process during launch windows. We'll document the SLA impact clearly.
[06:31] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Pricing timeline — when will we see the revised sheet?
[06:35] Maya Chen: I'll get it to you by EOD 2027-10-06. It will include 12-month committed pricing, burst addendum, and optional 18-month comparison.
[06:45] Sara Valdez: For SOC2 evidence, please include the last audit date and scope.
[06:50] Liam Ortiz: Will do. We'll also include the Private deployment checklist for your security team.
[06:56] Ethan Cole: On the technical run — what metrics will you report after the 48-hour benchmark?
[07:02] Liam Ortiz: We'll provide avg/median/p95/p99 latency, throughput (RPS), token throughput, GPU utilization, and a small quality report against your eval prompts. Also error rates and retry counts.
[07:14] Priya Nair: If the p99 in EU is still >250ms we need escalation — can we set an SLO at 250ms p99?
[07:22] Maya Chen: We can target p99 250ms for the EU pilot. Full production SLO may be slightly wider depending on model/context window but we'll aim for that.
[07:32] Sara Valdez: Also, legal wants a clause on data deletion timelines for PII.
[07:37] Maya Chen: We'll surface a data lifecycle clause in the contract addendum.
[07:41] Priya Nair: One small item — are model weights kept by Redwood or can we run certain models wholly on-prem?
[07:47] Liam Ortiz: For Private we can host models within your environment. Some third-party model licenses restrict redistribution — we'll call those out. For Redwood-curated open models, we can deploy them in your cluster.
[07:58] Ethan Cole: Good. That helps the compliance team.
[08:01] Maya Chen: Any final questions?
[08:03] Priya Nair: Not from me.
[08:05] Sara Valdez: No.
[08:06] Ethan Cole: Nothing else.
[08:07] Maya Chen: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pricing and docs.
[08:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality and artifacts: some auto-transcription mis-heard K V cache as "K V cash", and "Redwood Dedicated" occasionally came through as "Readwood Dedicated"; speaker overlaps at 05:30 caused minor attribution errors.

Referenced artifacts/links (to be shared):
- Pricing draft (to be emailed)
- SOC2/ISO artifacts (link)
- On-prem pilot checklist (doc)
- Replay trace export (Asterion to provide)

Pilot acceptance criteria (quick list):
- 48-hour benchmark meets p99 <= 250ms for EU pilot
- Error rate < 0.1% sustained
- Quality delta between primary model and fallback quantized variant <= 3% on eval set
- Secure KMS integration validated and logs retained inside eu-west region

End of transcript.
